* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
FFWSLC

The National Weather Service in Salt Lake City has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
West Central Kane County in southern Utah...
East Central Washington County in southwestern Utah...

* Until 100 AM MDT.

* At 1056 PM MDT, National Park Service reported flash flooding from
earlier thunderstorms producing heavy rain across Zion National
Park. A gauge at the North Fork of the Virgin River in Springdale
reported flows peaking over 5500 cfs at 800 PM MDT. The majority of
rainfall fell earlier, though a few storms are still in the area.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...National Park Service reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks, streams, slot
canyons, and normally dry washes.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Zion National Park, Springdale, Keyhole Canyon, Spry Canyon,
Parunuweap Canyon, the Narrows, Orderville Canyon, and the North
and East Forks of the Virgin River.

events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
FFWSLC

The National Weather Service in Salt Lake City has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
South Central Garfield County in southern Utah...
Northeastern Kane County in southern Utah...

* Until 100 AM MDT.

* At 1054 PM MDT, the river gauge on the Escalante River at Escalante
indicates flows stagnating around 2000 cfs, which will continue to
surge down the Escalante River. These flows stem from earlier
thunderstorms that produced heavy rain. The Flash Flood Warning has
been extended until 100 AM MDT. Flash flooding is already
occurring.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of the Escalante River.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
The Escalante River from near the town of Escalante to the terminus
at Lake Powell.

events.region: Kaibab Plateau; Marble and Glen Canyons
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of northern Coconino county, including the
following areas, Kaibab Plateau and Marble and Glen Canyons.

* WHEN...Until midnight MST /1 AM MDT/ tonight.

* IMPACTS...Flash flooding will be possible in creeks, normally dry
washes, swimming holes, and over recently burned areas. Raging
killer currents will be possible in side canyons and narrow slot
canyons. Low-water crossings may be flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Showers and thunderstorms are expected to continue this evening,
with deep monsoonal moisture in place and already saturated soils
in some locations.
- Additional information is available at weather.gov/flagstaff.

SMWLIX

The National Weather Service in New Orleans has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Coastal Waters from Port Fourchon LA to Lower Atchafalaya River LA
out 20 nm...
Coastal waters from Port Fourchon Louisiana to Lower Atchafalaya
River LA from 20 to 60 NM...
Terrebonne Bay...

* Until 100 AM CDT.

* At 1104 PM CDT, a cluster of severe thunderstorms capable of
producing waterspouts was located near Isle Derniers, moving
northwest at 45 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can quickly form and capsize boats...damage

Isle Derniers, Caillou Bay, and Timbalier Island.
